/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The previous Eventually loop was not properly checking if the pod was scheduled and running. Thus, the node name could not be retrieved from the pod specs. The plugin could not be retrieved and the UpdateStatus was called on a nil object.
TestPod function is now used instead, so the test waits for the pod to be scheduled. The Eventually loop to get the pod and resourceClaim is then no longer needed.

This is the number one test flake for DRA (the only one, actually).
I am currently looking into it. So far I managed to reproduce it twice (over 100+ runs), it seems to be due to the pod being not scheduled for some reason.

> it seems to be due to the pod being not scheduled for some reason.

that is odd, it seems there is code to wait for that

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3d342e9b74060b444dfff29a8ab9cb6601599510/test/e2e/dra/dra.go#L423-L430

what is updating this map?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3d342e9b74060b444dfff29a8ab9cb6601599510/test/e2e/dra/dra.go#L450

I will check there, and wait until that map is updated before doing the check, looks the race can be in that part
The 2 times it failed locally `scheduledPod.Spec.NodeName` was empty, not sure how it managed to go after the `gomega.Eventually` block you mentioned. `driver.Nodes` was correct.

> The 2 times it failed locally `scheduledPod.Spec.NodeName` was empty, not sure how it managed to go after the `gomega.Eventually` block you mentioned. `driver.Nodes` was correct.

are you sure is the same failure?

the stack trace indicates that it panics  on line 450, that IIUIC is when the map is accessed, most likely because the map was not initiliazed

>   k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/dra/test-driver/app.(*ExamplePlugin).UpdateStatus(0x476f900?, {0x7faf200beaa8, 0xc000dc7ce0}, 0xc006d7cd00)

I think it was the same issue as the Kubernetes CI, just I have very hard time to reproduce it (there might be flaky test for the DRA Admin feature). I have the same stack trace.

Why are you running those? Just focus on exactly the one test that you are debugging.

> This is the number one test flake for DRA (the only one, actually).

There is one more flake for Admin Access, but it has a fix pending (we just didn't merge because the feature is going to change anyway) and is super rare.

> > there might be flaky test for the DRA Admin feature
> 
> Why are you running those? Just focus on exactly the one test that you are debugging.

I run all DRA tests in parallel (I understand the CI does it like this, so I hoped I could reproduce the issue easily like that)
when there is a stack trace,  it should be possible to figure it out from the code when the map is initialized and check if it can happen that the map was not updated at the time of that check

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3d342e9b74060b444dfff29a8ab9cb6601599510/test/e2e/dra/dra.go#L450 can fail with a nil access if:
- `scheduledPod` is nil - should not happen because of the Eventually
- the selected `NodeName`  is not in `driver.Nodes` - should not happen, the pod can only get scheduled to nodes with a kubelet plugin
- `ExamplePlugin` is nil - should not happen, it [gets set for all map entries](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f0077a3689669018557de723a0416fda267d132f/test/e2e/dra/deploy.go#L441)

It cannot fail because of an uninitialized map, reading from a nil map is safe.

So one of those "should not happen" does happen. I would split up the expression into multiple lines, with one pointer access per line. Then a panic points to the exact one.

Also check that the map entry exists:
```Go
plugin, ok := driver.Nodes[scheduledPod.Spec.NodeName]
if !ok {
    framework.Failf("pod got scheduled to node %s without a plugin", scheduledPod.Spec.NodeName)
}
```

Sorry, I don't know what I did here, this seems very wrong.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3d342e9b74060b444dfff29a8ab9cb6601599510/test/e2e/dra/dra.go#L423-L430
I will fix that by using the testPod() function and I will do what you mentioned here:

> Also check that the map entry exists:

Here is the PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130285

> It cannot fail because of an uninitialized map, reading from a nil map is safe.

@pohly https://go.dev/play/p/jytq0Rq8gpQ
*Reading* is fine. But of course you then get a null entry, so *using* the entry may or may not crash, depending on what is supposed to be inside it.
